items.note: Association named, Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose organizer, main creamery 1891 (Story 1).
Article VII: paid on pounds of butterfat by test, not weight of milk; test at point of delivery governs (Story 1).
Story 2: 'Because payment was by test (Article VII) this was a running loss of real money, not a grievance of pride.'
Wilbur Teague bookkeeper and Hobart Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green named; Effie Loomis missing. List item with no REQUIRED line, so core fact credited.
Section A calls Selby Vose only the 'new manager' in 1919; never says he was Gideon's son or gives 1913 (son appears only in B3; D3 says 1911).

Stories 6-7: 'station gain' entries in the Association's ledgers; cream consistently ran heavier than the station's paperwork, 'always more, never less'. 1898 origin and 5.25% not given in A, but these are unbolded.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up-valley, winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
No description of the testing system (weighing, composite sample, percent read on bottle neck after fixed pipette charge) in Section A.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
$77.93 with the six dozen pipettes, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight; the 17.6 c.c. mark is in Story 8.
Story 2 gives a 0.19 gap that holds 'constantly, in every season, for a generation'; Story 8 says the fault was 'constant year-round'.
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette or that the county had none.
1861-1934, tester from the 1896 opening for twenty-nine seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925.
The station test book for all patrons, kept by Keddie in his own hand (Story 4).
Summary leaf never mentioned. 3.80 appears only as the 1958 'reconstructed true average', not as the 1896 recorded season. The step at the glassware change is not shown.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, borrowed measure, tests rose then fell back, question mark. The 3.80 figure is missing, but it is a list item with no REQUIRED line.
Married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, largest patron (Story 5).
1919 circular present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) is absent. Both bolded elements are required.
Died 1934 still under the county's suspicion.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant largest.
Gives 1 Jan 1897 or 1898, calls it unresolved, then weights r09's 1898 above r18. The key's 1 January 1897 is not established. Scales agreeing is present.
Gates on keeping the gaps apart. Story 2 resolves the Hollow-vs-elsewhere gap as 0.19 (and rejects 0.17), and Story 4 repeats the conflation, so the item is lost.
Grigg committee, January-March 1908 sampling, wet hay reported as the committee's explanation, not as fact.
200,000 lb at 3.42 is given, but the loss is treated as a flat 0.19 (3.42+0.19, 380 lb), which contradicts the proportional loss the key requires.
Passed to Roy on Emmet's 1929 death; lent by Roy to Ivy Keddie in 1958.
Alder Corners Cheese Company, Vessey County, 'over the ridge', Jerome Cudd founder. The ridge is not named Redlow.
Four of the six Hessel Bottom farms hauled there in the summer flush, 1915-1930.
Independent: own glassware, never compared figures, other county. At least two of the four elements.
Gives Alder Corners averages of 3.78-3.82 but never states that the same men tested about 0.19 higher there than at Ostrey Hollow in every overlapping season.
Story 7: the same patrons' milk tested elsewhere was never thin or watered, which disposes of both hay and watering.
Rosalie Cudd, daughter, ran the factory after 1941 and supplied Ivy the 1915-1930 run in 1958.
Merle Strawn never named in Section A and no circuit years are given there (F later says 1908).
Lactometer finding never water appears only in Section F, not A.
Inspector condemned the glassware 12 June 1923 (Story 8). The burette is not stated for 1923; list item with no REQUIRED line.
Nothing on Strawn writing no figure for the deficiency.
No replacement-glass dates, no 1924 average of 3.80, no 'nobody connected' in Section A.
Crate in the loft since 1923 is present, but the notebooks going to the college library in 1947 are absent. Both bolded elements are required.
Patrons petitioned January 1925.
Frick board, 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the station weigh room.
Watering (manager), cream skimming (Teague), wet hay (1908 report); board found no cause.
Four exhibits listed including the inspector's 1923 notebook, but A never says it contained the answer and was read for its other lines.
Dismissed 30 April 1925, board found no cause; $3,800 'without admission'. The account charged is scored at A7.6.
Section A never says the award was one fifth of $19,000 or that it was charged to the account holding the 'gain'.
Ivy Keddie b. 1931, granddaughter, State Agricultural College at Farland, Leland Vaught.
Section A never states that she assembled records never before in one room (that idea appears only in G).
February 1958, station loft, nine pipettes survived.
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, 16.72 vs 17.6, one part in twenty.
Every test in the same proportion from 1 May 1897 to 1923; 3.61 recorded against a true 3.80.
None of 40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 or the ledger identity appears in Section A.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, cleared twenty-four years after his death. The 35- and 33-year intervals are missing.
Granddaughter.
Duncan is Ansel's son and Ivy's father (r18).
Second cousins, derived via Duncan and Roy as first cousins.
Full vs half sibling declared unresolved and said not to change the answer. The lean toward Roy is explicitly 'a judgment call, not a proof'.
Gideon Vose.
Gideon wrote Article VII, which made the test decide pay; his son looked for the fault in the patrons rather than the equipment.
'None, on the weight of the evidence... I resolve for no relationship.' Asserts a verdict.
Asserting either way = 0. It also treats a family member's denial as decisive, the opposite of the key.
Adds a flat 0.19 to get a true test of 3.61 and 380 lb; key is 3.60 and 360 lb.
States about 1,520,000 lb actually received (reached by extrapolation, but the figure matches).
Gives 5.25% of credited (key 5.26%), and never gives 5.00% of delivered or the 76,000 lb difference here.
$77.93 with the itemized sum.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
Gives 'roughly 26 years', not 26 years and 6 weeks. The reason given (1896 excluded) is wrong; the part years are 1897 and 1923.
Abstains correctly: cannot be determined, two conflicting recollections.
Variable was the measuring instrument; own glass broken, borrowed measure used.
Herds, patrons, pasture/season, tester, supervision held constant.
Only 'rose markedly... fell back'. The 3.80 and 3.61 figures are not given.
Cause travels with the instrument, not milk/cows/patrons/tester; limit: does not give the size of the shortfall.
1911 interval (tester's book), ledger surplus (r02, r05, r07, r12, r23), Alder Corners (r10).
Argues independence across three record systems; all hold without the 1958 measurement.
Abstention item A09 answered 'No' (Teague never questioned the entries). Asserts a verdict.
Yes, he knew the station tested low: the complaints and his own 1919 circular.
Three of five: signed the ledger sheets with the station-gain line, wrote the 1919 circular, argued watering at the 1925 hearing (Section F). It also wrongly says manager from 1911.
No explicit declaration that A03 cannot be settled. Leans on Kyle's account and misses the opposing narrators, missing documents and the signature point. No verdict sentence, so no deduction.

Only row 2 (1908 sampling, report over covering letter) is found, resolved and given a method. Rows 3, 4, 8, 9, 12, 14, 15 are not addressed. Row 5 leans the wrong way, row 13 leans to eleven, and row 7 is resolved only in Section A.
Pairs noticed and broken: NT-9 $3,500 (r01, r21), NT-11 12 July (r08, r12), NT-15 five dozen (r11, r21), NT-16 eleven (r12, r19), NT-10, NT-5, NT-2. Capped at 3.
A04 asserted ('most plausibly... a mold was reground'). A06 not addressed. A10 abstention appears only in Section A. No credit in B-G.
r15's 'whole of 1908' against its own three-month report; r11's 16.27 against its own 'one part in twenty'.

Pipettes, 17.6/16.72, onset and cessation are given, but 0.19 is treated as a constant (added to Brant's 3.42 in C2 and Story 4), contradicting '0.19 is 5 percent of 3.80, not a constant'. The 1896 3.80 / 1924 3.80 onset-cessation figures are also not given.
Watering (Selby Vose) defeated by lactometer readings and Alder Corners tests.
Theft (Teague) defeated: the ledger shows cream arriving heavier, in his own hand.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's winter 0.05 and summer nothing, against a constant 0.19.
A07: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No.' Asserts a verdict.
A05: asserts that Keddie privately suspected the patrons, on Frick's account (also asserted in Story 5).
Summary is about 168 words, over the 150 cap.
Only four series named: ledgers, weigh book, inspector's notebook, 1958 bulletin. No invoice, test book, Alder Corners book, arbitration minutes or by-laws.
No decoy stated as fact and no wrong headline number (0.19, $19,000).
Only 1897, $19,000 and 1958 are present. No one-in-twenty, no 1923, no Ansel or Ivy named. Needs four.

deductions.reason: Corruption: Selby Vose manager 'from 1911' asserted as fact (D3)
Corruption: Strawn's lactometer tests 'from 1908 forward' asserted as fact (F, watering defeater)
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved 'no relationship' (B4, E17)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper never questioned the entries asserted ('No.') (D2)
Gullibility A07: board did not examine the glassware asserted ('No.') (F)
Gullibility A05: tester privately blamed the patrons asserted (F, Story 5)
Gullibility A04: short lot attributed to an accidental mold regrind ('most plausibly', no declining qualifier) (F unified theory)
